skill.name: laravel-security-audit
skill.description: Security auditor for Laravel applications that reviews code, configuration, and deployment risks using OWASP and Laravel practices.
skill.summary: Audit Laravel applications for common security risks and practical fixes.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives caused by Laravel security checklist language and a Markdown code fence. The skill does not request secrets, run commands, or perform network reconnaissance. No semantic evidence of prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or unsafe execution was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 220 is a Markdown PHP code fence followed by a Laravel query example, not Ruby backtick execution or shell execution. No command execution instruction or user-controlled shell input is present.
The text asks whether Laravel request()->all() is used dangerously during code review. It does not import an HTTP client, make a network call, or instruct live requests.
The line tells the auditor to review .env exposure risks, which is a defensive checklist item. It does not request reading, collecting, or revealing environment file contents.
The line asks whether a .env file is web-accessible as part of deployment review. This is defensive risk assessment, not environment file access or secret extraction.
Lines 31-32 list authorization correctness and secure configuration as audit priorities. They contain no reconnaissance workflow, targets, scanning instructions, or network probing.
Lines 33-34 mention OWASP awareness and realistic exploit scenarios for risk explanation. They do not instruct the agent to perform network reconnaissance or attack external systems.
Lines 75-76 list API abuse, rate bypass, and session hijacking as threats to consider in code review. The skill does not direct live testing or reconnaissance activity.

content.value_statement: Laravel applications can hide authorization, validation, and deployment weaknesses. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured security reviews.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Laravel validation, authorization, authentication, database, file upload, API, XSS, and deployment risks.
Identifies likely IDOR, mass assignment, raw query, CORS, debug, and .env exposure issues.
Classifies findings as critical, high, medium, low, or informational.
Explains realistic exploit scenarios when context supports them.
Recommends Laravel-native mitigations such as policies, gates, FormRequests, middleware, and scoped queries.
limitations: Requires the user to provide relevant Laravel code and configuration context.
Does not perform dynamic scanning, penetration testing, traffic capture, or live probing.
Findings need developer validation before production changes are applied.
Designed for Laravel backend security, not general feature implementation.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Find security regressions in Laravel controllers, routes, requests, policies, and models before merge.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Hardening
use_cases.description: Check deployment settings, debug exposure, CORS, HTTPS, trusted proxies, and environment file risks.

use_cases.title: Assess API Risk
use_cases.description: Evaluate authentication, throttling, sensitive fields, pagination limits, and authorization coverage for Laravel APIs.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Laravel Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one controller or route group.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Laravel code for validation, authorization, and data exposure issues. Classify each issue and suggest Laravel-native fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Check API Endpoint Security
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of API routes and controllers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these Laravel API routes and controllers for authentication, throttling, IDOR, sensitive fields, and unsafe request handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review File Upload Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this Laravel file upload flow for MIME checks, extension checks, storage location, executable upload risk, and size limits.

prompt_templates.title: Perform Release Security Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced pre-release review across code and configuration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Laravel release against OWASP risks, deployment settings, authentication, authorization, CORS, debug state, and .env exposure.

output_examples.input: A controller returns an order by user-supplied ID without ownership checks.
output: High risk IDOR because authenticated users may access other users orders.
Add a policy check or scope the query to the authenticated user.
Include an authorization test for cross-user access attempts.

output_examples.input: A production configuration summary shows debug enabled and broad CORS access.
output: High risk deployment misconfiguration because debug output may expose sensitive internals.
Disable debug in production and restrict CORS origins to trusted clients.
Verify HTTPS and trusted proxy settings before release.

output_examples.input: A file upload flow accepts images and stores them on a public disk.
output: Medium risk if MIME, extension, size, and executable content checks are incomplete.
Store uploads outside executable paths and serve them through controlled responses.
Add validation rules and tests for invalid file types.

best_practices: Provide routes, controllers, FormRequests, policies, middleware, models, and relevant configuration together.
State the environment, user roles, and expected access rules before requesting severity ratings.
Ask for exploit scenario, impact, and Laravel-native fix for each confirmed issue.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to probe live third-party systems or bypass authorization.
Do not paste secrets, tokens, passwords, or full environment file values.
Do not treat the output as a complete penetration test or compliance certification.

faq.question: What Laravel versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Laravel 10 and 11 applications, while many checks also apply to nearby versions.

faq.question: Can it review authentication and authorization code?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews policies, gates, middleware, controllers, token handling, and access control assumptions.

faq.question: Does it perform live security testing?
faq.answer: No. It is a code and configuration review aid, not a dynamic scanner or penetration testing tool.

faq.question: Should I paste my .env file?
faq.answer: No. Share relevant setting names or redacted values, but do not provide secrets.

faq.question: Can it provide fixed examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest Laravel-native fixes when enough code context is available.

faq.question: Is the audit output final security approval?
faq.answer: No. Use the findings as review guidance and validate changes with tests and human review.
